judged_text: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema lacks the uniqueness refinement that exists only in the client dialog's inline schema, so duplicate guests submitted directly through the API create duplicate attendee rows. A non-UI caller (or a stale client) posting {guests: ['a@b.com','a@b.com']} passes validation, createMany inserts two identical attendees, the calendar event and emails then list the guest twice — the client-only refine silently changed the contract by not being lifted into the shared schema.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the submitted `guests` array, so `['a@b.com','a@b.com']` remains duplicated and is passed to `createMany`, which will attempt to create two identical attendee rows. The client dialog adds a uniqueness `refine`, but that is not shared/enforced on the server, so non-UI callers or stale clients can trigger duplicates.
